newsitem.title: USA: U.S. to process Iraq oil licenses "expeditiously".
newsitem.headline: U.S. to process Iraq oil licenses "expeditiously".

text.p: The U.S. Treasury Department's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) said Tuesday it will "expeditiously process" license applications for U.S. firms seeking to buy Iraqi oil.

In regulations issued on Iraq oil licenses, the OFAC said U.S. firms that signed executory contracts to buy Iraqi oil under a previously issued OFAC general license now will be able to request specific licenses. That will place them on the list for direct dealings with the United Nations committee in charge of the sales.

U.S. applicants for specific licenses under the U.N.'s oil-for-food plan for Iraq must submit basic business information, and written certification that they have entered into an executory oil purchase contract with Iraq, the OFAC statement said.

Applicants also must show they fully understand and will abide by all applicable U.S. and U.N. rules, and acknowledge that as licensees they will promptly provide OFAC information on their dealings with Iraq on demand.
The regulations generally license all U.S. persons and firms to enter into secondary oil purchase agreements with any primary purchaser previously authorized by the U.N., the OFAC statement said.
"OFAC will expeditiously process applications and provide the resulting list of licensees to the administering U.N. committee," an agency fact sheet on the regulations said.

It said specific licenses also are available to U.S. firms that have signed executory contracts to sell humanitarian goods such as food and medicine, or essential pipeline equipment, to Iraq through U.N. procedures.
Copies of contracts with Iraq and other information must be provided to OFAC, the office said.
